protocol: TJ Compassion + L.O.V.E. — sources recorded against UniProt / PubChem / ClinVar / OMIM / FDA / Orphanet

disease.inheritance: Autosomal recessive — biallelic GAA trinucleotide repeat expansion in intron 1 of FXN
disease.mechanism: Loss-of-function. The expanded GAA repeat in FXN intron 1 forms a triplex/heterochromatin structure that impedes transcription elongation and induces locus-specific transcriptional silencing of FXN. This reduces frataxin to ~5-30% of normal, impairing mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster (ISC) biogenesis and leading to iron accumulation and oxidative stress.
disease.autotac_rationale: NOT eligible. FRDA is a loss-of-function disease — frataxin is depleted, not accumulated. Degrading frataxin further would worsen the disease. Correct route is frataxin restoration (upregulators, gene therapy), not protein degradation.
disease.prevalence: 1–9 per 100,000 (Orphanet); ~1 in 20,000–1 in 50,000 in people of Caucasian descent
disease.age_of_onset: Typically 5-15 years (gait ataxia); can be later in milder forms

approved_treatments.mechanism_correct: Activates the Nrf2 antioxidant pathway, reducing oxidative stress and improving mitochondrial function. It does NOT restore frataxin expression directly; it mitigates downstream oxidative damage.
approved_treatments.note: First FDA-approved therapy for FRDA (2023). Slows decline; not curative.

investigational: Etravirine (NNRTI) — reported to increase frataxin expression (Phase 2 FAEST1, NCT04273165, COMPLETED Jan 2023)
Histone deacetylase inhibitors (e.g. HDAC3) — preclinical frataxin upregulation

disease.human_summary: Friedreich ataxia is the most common hereditary ataxia. Progressive gait and limb ataxia, dysarthria, and cardiomyopathy typically begin in adolescence. Most cases are caused by a GAA repeat expansion that silences frataxin, a mitochondrial protein needed for iron-sulfur cluster assembly.
disease.clinical_trials_note: 12 curated interventional trials; 115 ClinicalTrials.gov studies in total (2026-11-07)
disease.uk_access: MHRA approved omaveloxolone on 2025-04-23. NICE TA1061 was terminated on 2025-05-06 after Biogen withdrew. SMC2845 did not recommend it on 2026-03-09. Not routinely available on the NHS; individual funding routes are discretionary.
disease.structural_note: PDB 3T3K is the Q148R disease-variant construct covering residues 82–210; it is not wild-type frataxin or the full 210-residue precursor.
